clue.text: Get modern gas fitted, taking care of finance agreement

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take something in, holding it inside themselves
things fitted are put into place and arranged, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A homeowner borrows money to have modern gas fitted, signing a finance deal to cover it.
explanation.definitionFit: A second mortgage is a further loan secured on a property already mortgaged, a kind of finance agreement.

clue.text: Coy at first, as 'worried well'

definitions.note: adverb in the clue, read as the adjective in 'all is well'

indicators.note: something worried is pulled about and disturbed, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shy patient, one of the 'worried well', who fret about health though they are fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'worried well' are healthy people anxious about illness; here 'worried' acts on the words before it and 'well' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying things are well means they are in acceptable condition, which is what satisfactory describes.

clue.text: Stroke stomach, then pound

parts.note: a craw is a bird's crop, used loosely for the stomach
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone gently strokes a belly and then gives it a thump.
explanation.definitionFit: The crawl is a swimming stroke, the front stroke used in freestyle racing.

clue.text: Barely awake, every fool avoiding smack

parts.note: if every one avoids something, then none suffers it, so the sentence is restated with 'no'
a twit is a silly person
to smack someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: A sleepy person, apparently in a world where every idiot dodges a slap.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a paraphrase: if every fool avoids a smack, then 'no twit (is) hit', and those words run together give NOT WITH IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not with it is dazed or slow to grasp things, as a person barely awake would be.

clue.text: Robs house: tense, one's taken by police

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them in the street
HO is the abbreviation for house
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A burglar robs a house while tense, and is then taken in by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken by police' reads like an arrest, but it is a photograph that is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugshot is the photograph police take of a person after arrest.

clue.text: Sort of van band's taken to test match?

parts.note: R.E.M. was an American rock band
the Oval is a London cricket ground that hosts test matches

explanation.surface: A group's gear is driven to a cricket test match in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: A test match is an international cricket match; the clue gives the venue rather than the event, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A removal van carries a household's furniture when people move house.

clue.text: What Bill has protecting his mansion?

definitions.text: What Bill has protecting his mansion?

parts.words: What Bill has protecting his mansion?
parts.note: surface reading: the security barriers at the entrance to some Bill's large house
setter's reading: Bill is the Microsoft founder, so what he has is his own surname

explanation.walkthrough: Bill seems to be any rich homeowner; read him as the Microsoft billionaire and his surname also names the barriers across a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Gates are hinged barriers closing an entrance, and also the surname of the billionaire Bill.

clue.text: Good: paid attention and shone

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to listen is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A model pupil was good, attentive and brilliant in class.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to sparkle with reflected light, a synonym of shining.

clue.text: Health food?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a drink raised to someone's health
second meaning: browned slices of bread

explanation.walkthrough: 'Health food' is a fixed phrase, but split it: a drink raised to someone's health, and a food, are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is a drink proposed in honour of someone's health, and toast is also browned bread.

clue.text: Drop pounds in a sort of progression, losing energy

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a geometric progression is a sequence with a constant ratio
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dieter sheds pounds steadily, as in a mathematical progression, but runs out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop pounds' suggests weight loss; the pounds are the imperial units abandoned on going metric.
explanation.definitionFit: To go metric is to switch from imperial measures such as pounds to kilograms and metres.

clue.text: Already settled before gig, edged to the sides

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a gig is a live music performance

indicators.note: only the parts at the sides are wanted, so the two end letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A band's arrangements were all sorted before the gig, with the stage edged at the sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Preconcerted means arranged or agreed in advance, so already settled.

clue.text: Heedless of others, fairy lives in peace

indicators.note: these pieces sit inside another, held within it

parts.note: sh! is a call for quiet
an elf is a small fairy
to be or exist, as 'lives' can mean

explanation.surface: A fairy lives peacefully, oblivious to everyone around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish person cares only for themselves, without regard to the needs of others.

clue.text: Tourist in India finally got covered in sunscreen

indicators.note: something covered in another is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: a visor shields the eyes from the sun
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tourist in India ends up slathered in sun cream.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunscreen suggests lotion, but here it is a peaked shade worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a visitor, someone who comes to a place for a stay or sightseeing.

clue.text: I slipped into opening, dropping this at the start?

definitions.text: I slipped into opening, dropping this at the start?

indicators.note: something slipped into another is put inside it
dropping a letter means leaving it out, here from the front

parts.note: a hatch is an opening in a deck or wall
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slips through a hatchway, dropping their aitches as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the answer itself: the letter H, spelt AITCH, is what is dropped from the start of HATCH before I goes in, as when people say 'atch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H, the letter that is dropped from the word.

clue.text: Record of passing summertime with cat I carried round

indicators.note: carried round means taken around something, so these pieces surround another

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
BST is British Summer Time
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A summer outing in which someone carries a cat around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombstone marks a grave, recording a person's death, which is their passing.

clue.text: Good to goggle at?

parts.note: surface reading: something pleasant to stare at
setter's reading: the goggle-box is slang for television, so good to watch on screen

explanation.walkthrough: The goggle-box is British slang for a television set, so goggling here means watching TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegenic person looks attractive on television, appealing to viewers watching the screen.

clue.text: Lunch spot to grab and sup, relaxing

indicators.note: relaxing loosens what was tight, letting the letters fall into a different order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
more letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A place to grab lunch and have a drink while taking it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub that serves restaurant-quality food, a popular place to eat lunch.

clue.text: Multiplication aid ignored by son in a series of lessons

indicators.note: something ignored is passed over, so this letter is left out

parts.note: children learn multiplication from a times table
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy skips his multiplication practice during a run of school lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A school timetable sets out the series of lessons through the week.

clue.text: Homeless person happy in Morecambe, for one

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, held within it

parts.note: Morecambe Bay is an example of a bay, on the Lancashire coast
glad means happy

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping rough who is happy living in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a seaside town in Lancashire, but 'for one' asks for what kind of thing it is: the bay it stands on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag lady is a homeless woman who carries her possessions around in bags.

clue.text: Facial hair say I stroke

indicators.note: say means speak the word, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

parts.note: the letter I is pronounced like the organ of sight
a lash is a stroke of a whip

explanation.surface: Someone offers to stroke a beard or moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelash is one of the hairs growing on the edge of the eyelid, on the face.

clue.text: In fine weather, departs a divided country

indicators.note: the following pieces go inside, held within the first

parts.note: sunshine is fine weather
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
taken as written

explanation.surface: When the weather turns fine, someone leaves a country split by conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan was divided in 2011 when South Sudan seceded to become an independent country.

clue.text: Contacted over the way one's showing deterioration

indicators.note: over means lying across and around, so this word encloses the rest

parts.note: rung is the past participle of ring, to phone someone
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the Roman numeral for one; the 's is read as 'is' and joins to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone got in touch about the road, which is in a bad state of repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusting metal is corroding, visibly deteriorating as rust forms on it.

clue.text: Fly for one not caught in loose sheet

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letter is taken away

parts.note: a fly is an example of an insect
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fly escapes capture inside a loose bedsheet.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is an extra page or leaflet placed loose inside a magazine or book.

clue.text: In pain, nameless compiler going on leave at last

indicators.note: going on means following on after, so the compiler piece is placed after the other
at last points to the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

indicators.note: nameless means lacking a name, so the abbreviation for name is removed

parts.note: Arachne is a Guardian crossword compiler
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A setter, who must stay anonymous, suffers as they head off on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The compiler is Arachne, another setter of the Guardian crossword, named after the spinner of myth; 'going on' places her after the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a specific kind of pain, felt in the ear.

clue.text: What priest may wear in bed, half so long

indicators.note: only half of the phrase is wanted, so the other half is dropped

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
ta-ta is a casual British goodbye

explanation.surface: A priest's nightwear, worn in bed, cut to half the usual length.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short white surplice worn by priests and choristers over a cassock.

clue.text: From within rocky boat elegant bird makes land

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, surrounded by it
something rocky is unsteady and tossed about, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the swan is proverbially graceful

explanation.surface: A graceful bird flies off from a rocking boat and comes to land.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa, so a land in the sense of a nation.

clue.text: Make a fuss of something small

parts.note: to pet an animal is to stroke and fuss over it
it stands for a thing in general

explanation.surface: An instruction to spoil some little creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something small' reads as one phrase, but 'something' belongs to the wordplay and 'small' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit is French for little and survives in English phrases like petit four and petit bourgeois.

clue.text: Passed the table and was ignored

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: board is an old word for a table, so this is moving past one
second meaning, idiomatic: something that goes by the board is abandoned or disregarded

explanation.walkthrough: Board meaning table survives in 'bed and board'; the idiom originally meant falling overboard past a ship's side.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by the board is an idiom for being neglected or discarded, and literally means passing a board or table.
